title: You Don't Need Flights to See China's Northwest — One 3,000 km Loop | China Travel Expert
description:
Most people picture a dozen flights to see China's wild northwest. You don't need them — it's one road loop, about 3,000 km, that starts and ends in a single city.

The Qinghai–Gansu Grand Loop (青甘大环线) begins and ends in Xining, the capital of Qinghai, and runs roughly 3,000 km over 7–10 days, mostly by road. In one circle it strings together a high-altitude lake that mirrors the sky, rainbow-striped rock hills, wide grasslands under snow peaks, and singing sand dunes with a desert spring — the kind of variety most travellers assume needs separate trips and multiple flights.

🧭 Expert Tip: time it for July — the Menyuan rapeseed fields on the loop bloom into a gold carpet against the Qilian mountains.
